lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: God creates the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them, in six days, and rests on the seventh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God made on each day, and what happened on the seventh?
ev: Retell what God made on each of the six days
Say that God rested on the seventh day and blessed it

nodes.t: Made in the image of God
nodes.d: Man and woman are made in God's image and given dominion; the same truth grounds the sanctity of human life after the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 1:26-27 teaches about people, and why this matters?
ev: Explain what it means to be made in God's image using Genesis 1:26-27
Connect Genesis 9:6 to the value of human life

nodes.d: God plants a garden, places the man in it with a command, and forms the woman as a helper fit for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the garden and the one thing God told the man not to do?
ev: Retell the formation of the man and the woman
State God's command about the tree (2:16-17)

nodes.d: The serpent tempts the woman; she and the man eat the fruit God forbade and hide from God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how sin entered the world in Genesis 3?
ev: Retell the temptation and the disobedience in order
Explain what the man and woman did when God called

nodes.t: The curse and the first promise
nodes.d: God pronounces judgment, yet promises that the woman's offspring will bruise the serpent's head (3:15), and clothes the man and woman before sending them from the garden.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the promise in Genesis 3:15?
ev: Name the consequences God gives in 3:14-19
Read 3:15 and say why it is called the first promise of a saviour

nodes.d: Cain murders his brother Abel after God accepts Abel's offering and not his own.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Cain did and how God responded?
ev: Retell the story, including God's question to Cain (4:9)

nodes.t: Cain's line and the birth of Seth
nodes.d: Cain builds a city and his descendants include tent-dwellers, musicians and metalworkers, while Lamech boasts of killing a man. Adam and Eve have Seth in place of Abel, and in Seth's day men begin to call on the name of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Genesis 4 ends with two family lines, Cain's and Seth's, and what is said about Seth's son Enos?
ev: Name some of Cain's descendants and what they were known for (4:20-22)
Contrast Lamech's words in 4:23-24 with the birth of Seth and the calling on the LORD's name in 4:25-26

nodes.t: From Adam to Noah: the first genealogy
nodes.d: Genesis 5 lists ten generations from Adam to Noah, repeating that each one lived a number of years and died, except Enoch, who walked with God and was not, for God took him. Lamech names his son Noah with a hope of comfort from the cursed ground.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 5 tells us about Enoch, and why the chapter keeps repeating that each man died?
ev: Point out the repeated phrase 'and he died' in the chapter and the one exception in verse 24
Explain what Lamech hoped for when he named Noah (5:29)

nodes.t: The sons of God and the daughters of men
nodes.d: As men multiply, the sons of God take wives of the daughters of men, and the LORD limits man's days to one hundred and twenty years. The text notes mighty men of renown born in those days.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what Genesis 6:1-4 says, and explain why the identity of the 'sons of God' needs careful study of the text?
ev: Summarise what Genesis 6:1-4 reports happening and what the LORD says in 6:3
Say honestly which points in the passage are plainly stated and which are debated

nodes.d: God sees the wickedness of man, finds favour with Noah, and saves him and his household in the ark through the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Noah and the ark?
ev: Retell why God sent the flood and how Noah and his family were saved
Say how Noah left the ark and what he did (8:20)

nodes.t: A new start: blessing, food and the sanctity of life
nodes.d: After the flood God blesses Noah and his sons, tells them to be fruitful, puts the animals under their hand, permits meat but not blood, and requires an account for the shedding of man's blood because man is made in God's image.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why God says in Genesis 9:6 that shedding man's blood is so serious?
ev: List what God tells Noah's family to do and what He permits and forbids in 9:1-5
Explain the reason given in 9:6 for the penalty for shedding man's blood

nodes.d: After the flood God establishes his covenant with Noah and every living creature and sets the rainbow as its sign.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what God promised Noah and what the sign was?
ev: State what God promises in 9:11
Identify the sign of the covenant (9:12-13)

nodes.t: Noah's vineyard and the curse on Canaan
nodes.d: Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk and lies uncovered in his tent. Ham tells his brothers, while Shem and Japheth cover their father, and Noah then curses Canaan and blesses the LORD God of Shem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened in Noah's tent and how Shem, Ham and Japheth each responded?
ev: Contrast what Ham did with what Shem and Japheth did (9:22-23)
State exactly whom Noah curses and whom he blesses (9:25-27)

nodes.d: Genesis 10 traces the families of Japheth, Ham and Shem after the flood, naming nations, lands and tongues, including Nimrod's kingdom beginning at Babel. It closes by saying the nations were divided in the earth after the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Genesis 10 teaches about where the nations came from?
ev: Name Noah's three sons and one nation or person listed under each
Find where Nimrod and Babel appear in the chapter (10:8-10)

nodes.d: The people build a city and tower; God confuses their language and scatters them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Babel?
ev: Retell why the people built the tower and what God did

nodes.d: A second genealogy runs from Shem to Terah and his sons Abram, Nahor and Haran. It notes that Haran died in Ur, that Sarai was barren, and that Terah set out for Canaan but settled in Haran, where he died.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Genesis 11:10-32 introduces Abram and Sarai, and why Sarai's barrenness matters?
ev: Trace the line from Shem to Abram in 11:10-26
Say what is told about Sarai in 11:30 and where Terah's journey stopped (11:31-32)

nodes.d: God calls Abram to leave his country and promises to make him a great nation and bless all the families of the earth through him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God promised Abram in Genesis 12:1-3?
ev: State the promises of 12:1-3
Say that Abram went as the LORD told him

nodes.d: A famine sends Abram down to Egypt, where he asks Sarai to say she is his sister for fear of being killed. Pharaoh takes her, the LORD plagues his house, and Pharaoh sends Abram away with his wife and all he had.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened in Egypt and say who protected Sarai?
ev: Explain why Abram told Sarai to say she was his sister (12:11-13)
Say who acts to rescue Sarai (12:17)

nodes.d: Abram returns to Bethel and calls on the LORD. Strife between the herdmen leads Abram to offer Lot his choice of land; Lot chooses the plain near Sodom, and the LORD then renews the promise of land and seed to Abram.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Abram handled the quarrel with Lot, and what God promised him afterward?
ev: Describe how Abram settled the quarrel and what Lot chose
Say what the LORD promises Abram after Lot leaves (13:14-17)

nodes.d: Four kings defeat the kings of the plain and carry off Lot with his goods. Abram arms 318 trained servants, pursues them by night and brings back Lot, the goods and the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Abram went after the four kings and what he recovered?
ev: Explain why Abram went to war (14:12-14)
Describe how he pursued and what he brought back (14:14-16)

nodes.d: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, brings bread and wine and blesses Abram, who gives him tithes of all. Abram refuses the king of Sodom's goods, saying he has lifted his hand to the LORD, the most high God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Melchizedek did for Abram and what Abram gave him?
ev: Say who Melchizedek is according to 14:18 and what he does and says
Explain why Abram refuses to take anything from the king of Sodom (14:22-23)

nodes.t: Abram believed and it was counted as righteousness
nodes.d: Genesis 15:6 records that Abram believed the LORD and it was counted to him as righteousness, the verse Paul explains in Romans 4.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Genesis 15:6 in their own words?
ev: Quote or paraphrase 15:6 accurately
Say who or what Abram believed

nodes.d: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?
ev: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed

nodes.t: Hagar and the birth of Ishmael
nodes.d: Sarai, still childless, gives her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram; Hagar conceives and is treated harshly and flees. The angel of the LORD finds her at a spring, tells her to return, promises many descendants and names her son Ishmael, and she calls God the one who sees her.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened to Hagar in the wilderness and what she learned about God?
ev: Explain how Hagar came to be Abram's wife (16:1-3)
Tell what the angel of the LORD says to Hagar and what she calls the LORD (16:7-13)

nodes.d: God appears to Abram at ninety-nine, changes his name to Abraham, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what circumcision was a sign of in Genesis 17?
ev: Explain the name change (17:5)
State what circumcision signified (17:10-11)

nodes.t: The LORD visits Abraham and Sarah
nodes.d: The LORD appears to Abraham in the plains of Mamre as three men; Abraham hurries to feed them. One says Sarah will have a son at the appointed time, Sarah laughs inside the tent, and the LORD asks whether anything is too hard for Him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the visitors promised Sarah and why she laughed?
ev: Describe Abraham's hospitality to the three men (18:2-8)
Repeat the question the LORD asks in 18:14 and say what it is about

nodes.d: The LORD tells Abraham He will see whether the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is as great as it seems. Abraham draws near and asks whether the Judge of all the earth will do right, and the LORD agrees to spare the city for fifty, then down to ten righteous.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Abraham asked the LORD about Sodom and how the LORD answered?
ev: Say why the LORD decides to tell Abraham what He will do (18:17-19)
Trace the numbers Abraham names and the LORD's answers (18:24-32)

nodes.d: Two angels come to Lot in Sodom, the men of the city press against his house, and the angels strike them with blindness. They lead Lot, his wife and daughters out; the LORD rains brimstone and fire on the cities and Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Lot was brought out of Sodom and what happened to the cities?
ev: Describe how the angels protected Lot and urged him to leave (19:10-17)
Say what God did to the cities and why 19:29 says He remembered Abraham

nodes.t: Lot's daughters and the birth of Moab and Ammon
nodes.d: Lot goes up out of Zoar to live in a cave with his two daughters. Fearing no man remains to give them children, they make their father drunk and conceive sons, Moab and Ben-ammi, who become the fathers of the Moabites and Ammonites.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say which nations descend from Lot's daughters according to Genesis 19:30-38?
ev: State the origin of the Moabites and Ammonites as given in 19:37-38
Observe how the text reports the daughters' plan without commending it

nodes.d: In Gerar, Abraham again calls Sarah his sister and King Abimelech takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream that he is a dead man, withheld him from sin, and tells him to restore her, for Abraham is a prophet who will pray for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how God protected Sarah in Gerar and what Abraham's reason was for saying she was his sister?
ev: Explain how God intervened to keep Abimelech from touching Sarah (20:3-6)
Say what Abraham does for Abimelech at the end of the chapter (20:17-18)

nodes.d: God keeps his promise: Sarah bears Isaac to Abraham in his old age.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Isaac was born?
ev: Retell how God kept his promise

nodes.t: Hagar and Ishmael are sent away
nodes.d: After Isaac is weaned, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and asks that he and Hagar be cast out. God tells Abraham that his seed will be called in Isaac but he will also make a nation of Ishmael; in the wilderness God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised about Ishmael, even as Isaac was the child of promise?
ev: Say what God told Abraham in 21:12-13
Describe how God provided for Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness (21:17-20)

nodes.d: Abimelech and Phichol ask Abraham to swear he will not deal falsely with them. Abraham reproves Abimelech about a seized well, the two make a covenant with seven ewe lambs as a witness, and Abraham calls on the name of the LORD, the everlasting God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the well at Beersheba led to a covenant between Abraham and Abimelech?
ev: Explain why Abraham set apart seven ewe lambs (21:28-30)
Say how Beersheba got its name (21:31)

nodes.d: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac; God provides a ram in his place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God provided on the mountain?
ev: Retell the story, including 22:8 and 22:13-14

nodes.d: Abraham sends his eldest servant under oath to his own kindred to find a wife for Isaac, not from the Canaanites. At the well the servant prays, Rebekah, a granddaughter of Abraham's brother Nahor, answers the sign, and after her family agrees she goes with him and marries Isaac.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Abraham's servant found Rebekah and who he said had guided him?
ev: Retell the servant's prayer at the well and how Rebekah answered it (24:12-20)
Point to places where the servant and Laban and Bethuel credit the LORD (24:27, 24:50)

nodes.d: Sarah dies in Hebron, and Abraham, calling himself a stranger and sojourner, negotiates with the sons of Heth to buy the cave of Machpelah from Ephron for four hundred shekels of silver. He buries Sarah there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Abraham came to own a piece of the promised land?
ev: Describe how Abraham obtained the burial place and what he paid (23:8-16)
Explain why a purchase of land in Canaan is notable in view of God's promise (cf. 13:15)

nodes.d: Abraham takes Keturah, gives all he has to Isaac and gifts to his other sons, and dies at one hundred and seventy-five. Isaac and Ishmael bury him at Machpelah, God blesses Isaac, and the generations of Ishmael's twelve princes are listed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened after Abraham died and how God treated Isaac?
ev: Say who inherited Abraham's possessions and who buried him (25:5, 25:9)
Count the sons of Ishmael called princes (25:13-16)

nodes.d: Esau sells his birthright to Jacob, and Jacob later receives Isaac's blessing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob received the birthright and the blessing?
ev: Retell the birthright and blessing episodes
Note God's word to Rebekah in 25:23

nodes.d: In a famine the LORD tells Isaac not to go to Egypt and repeats the promise made to Abraham. Isaac calls Rebekah his sister, is rebuked by Abimelech, prospers, digs wells that herdsmen contest, and the LORD appears at Beersheba before Abimelech makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how God renewed His promise to Isaac and what happened with the wells?
ev: Compare Isaac's words about Rebekah with Abraham's in chapters 12 and 20
Name the three wells Isaac dug after Gerar and what each name recalls (26:20-22)

nodes.d: Isaac blesses Jacob, charges him not to marry a Canaanite and sends him to Laban's house for a wife, with the blessing of Abraham. Esau, seeing this, marries a daughter of Ishmael.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jacob was sent away to Laban and what Isaac asked God to give him?
ev: State what Isaac charges Jacob and the blessing he pronounces (28:1-4)
Say what Esau does in response (28:6-9)

nodes.d: Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven, and the LORD renews the promise to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe Jacob's dream and what God promised?
ev: Retell the dream
State the promise in 28:13-15

nodes.d: At a well Jacob meets Rachel and serves Laban seven years for her, but Laban gives him Leah first and Jacob serves seven more for Rachel. The LORD sees that Leah is hated and opens her womb, and she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob came to marry both Leah and Rachel and what the LORD did for Leah?
ev: Describe the deception on the wedding night and how Laban explained it (29:23-27)
Name Leah's four sons and note which one is Judah (29:32-35)

nodes.t: Jacob's sons are born and his flocks increase
nodes.d: Rachel and Leah compete, giving their maids to Jacob, and sons are born including Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun and Dinah. God remembers Rachel and she bears Joseph; Jacob then bargains with Laban over the flocks and grows exceedingly rich.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the family of Jacob grew in Haran and which son was born to Rachel?
ev: Match each son with his mother as the chapter reports (Bilhah, Zilpah, Leah, Rachel)
Describe the wages Jacob proposed to Laban and the result (30:31-43)

nodes.d: After Laban's sons complain and Laban's face turns against him, the LORD tells Jacob to return to his kindred. Jacob leaves in secret, Rachel takes her father's household images, and Laban pursues him but is warned by God in a dream not to speak good or bad; the two make a covenant with a heap of stones.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jacob left Laban secretly and how God kept him safe?
ev: Say what God told Jacob in 31:3 and 31:13
Explain how God protected Jacob when Laban caught up with him (31:24, 31:42)

nodes.d: Angels of God meet Jacob at Mahanaim. Hearing that Esau is coming with four hundred men, Jacob divides his company, prays to the God of Abraham and Isaac, reminding Him of His promise, and sends droves of animals ahead as a present.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob responded when he heard Esau was coming with four hundred men?
ev: Summarise Jacob's prayer in 32:9-12 and note what promises he recalls
Describe the present he sent to Esau and why (32:13-20)

nodes.t: Jacob wrestles and is named Israel
nodes.d: Jacob wrestles with a man until daybreak and is given the name Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob became Israel?
ev: Retell the wrestling and the new name

nodes.d: Jacob bows seven times as Esau runs to embrace him, and the two weep. Jacob urges Esau to accept the present, they part, and Jacob settles near Shechem, buys a field and raises an altar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Jacob and Esau finally met after so many years?
ev: Describe how Esau greeted Jacob in 33:4
Say what Jacob did when he arrived near Shechem (33:18-20)

nodes.t: Dinah and the men of Shechem
nodes.d: Shechem takes Dinah and defiles her, then asks to marry her. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully and demand circumcision; on the third day Simeon and Levi kill the males of the city, and Jacob rebukes them for troubling him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Simeon and Levi did at Shechem and how their father responded?
ev: Explain how the sons of Jacob used circumcision to deceive the men of Shechem (34:13-25)
Note Jacob's reaction in 34:30 and what the text reports of Simeon and Levi's reply

nodes.t: Back to Bethel: God confirms Israel's name
nodes.d: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel; Jacob has his household put away their strange gods. At Bethel God blesses him, repeats that his name is Israel, and renews the promise of nations and land; Rachel dies bearing Benjamin, and Isaac dies at one hundred and eighty.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God said to Jacob at Bethel in Genesis 35 and who the twelve sons of Jacob were?
ev: Say what Jacob told his household to do before going to Bethel (35:2-4)
List the twelve sons of Jacob by their mothers (35:22-26)

nodes.t: The generations of Esau, who is Edom
nodes.d: Genesis 36 lists Esau's wives, sons and chiefs, notes that he moved to Mount Seir because the land could not bear both his and Jacob's herds, and lists the Horite families and the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the Edomites came from according to Genesis 36?
ev: Find the verse that says Esau is Edom and the verse that says why he moved (36:1, 36:6-8)
Point out the phrase about kings reigning before any king ruled Israel (36:31)

nodes.t: Joseph is sold by his brothers
nodes.d: Joseph's brothers hate him and sell him to traders who take him to Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Joseph's brothers sold him?
ev: Retell the story from the dreams to the sale

nodes.d: Judah's sons Er and Onan die, and he withholds his third son Shelah from Tamar. Tamar disguises herself, conceives by Judah, produces his signet, cord and staff, and Judah says she is more righteous than he; she bears twins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Judah says Tamar was more righteous than he was?
ev: Say what Tamar did and what proof she showed Judah (38:14-25)
Quote or state Judah's verdict in 38:26 and say why he gives it

nodes.d: Joseph is bought by Potiphar in Egypt, and the LORD is with him so that all prospers in his hand. When Potiphar's wife presses him he refuses as a great wickedness before God; she falsely accuses him and he is put in prison, where the LORD is still with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Joseph did when Potiphar's wife tempted him and what happened to him afterward?
ev: Give Joseph's reason for refusing Potiphar's wife (39:8-9)
Note how often the chapter says the LORD was with Joseph (39:2, 39:21, 39:23)

nodes.t: The butler and the baker's dreams
nodes.d: In prison Joseph serves Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker, who each dream. Saying that interpretations belong to God, Joseph tells the butler he will be restored and the baker hanged; it happens in three days, but the butler forgets Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joseph interpreted the two prisoners' dreams and who he said gives interpretations?
ev: Compare the two dreams and Joseph's interpretations (40:9-19)
Say what Joseph asks of the butler and what happens (40:14, 40:23)

nodes.t: Joseph is raised up in Egypt
nodes.d: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is set over the land of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joseph came to rule in Egypt?
ev: Retell the dreams and what Joseph advised

nodes.d: In the famine Jacob sends ten sons to buy grain in Egypt while keeping Benjamin at home. Joseph recognises them and remembers his dreams, accuses them of spying, binds Simeon and sends the rest home with the demand to bring Benjamin; their money is found in their sacks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph demanded of his brothers and why they said they were guilty?
ev: Point to 42:6-9 and say why the brothers do not know Joseph but he knows them
Say what the brothers admit to one another in 42:21-22

nodes.d: With the grain eaten, Judah promises to be surety for Benjamin, and Jacob reluctantly lets him go with a gift and double money. Joseph has the brothers brought to his house for a meal, weeps in his chamber on seeing Benjamin, and serves Benjamin five times as much.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob was persuaded to send Benjamin and what Joseph did when he saw him?
ev: Say what Judah offers his father in 43:8-9
Describe Joseph's reaction on seeing Benjamin (43:29-31)

nodes.t: The silver cup and Judah's plea
nodes.d: Joseph has his silver cup put in Benjamin's sack and sends his steward after the brothers. When the cup is found Judah pleads with Joseph, tells how Jacob loves the boy, and offers himself as a bondman in Benjamin's place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Judah offered to do for Benjamin and why?
ev: Explain how the cup came to be in Benjamin's sack (44:1-2, 44:12)
Summarise Judah's offer and the reason he gives (44:32-34)

nodes.d: Joseph cannot hold back and tells his brothers he is Joseph, saying not to be grieved that they sold him, for God sent him before them to preserve life. Pharaoh invites the family to Egypt, and Jacob's spirit revives when he hears Joseph is alive.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Joseph understood what had happened to him and what he told his brothers?
ev: Retell what Joseph says in 45:4-8 about who sent him to Egypt
Say how Jacob reacted to the news (45:26-28)

nodes.d: At Beersheba God tells Israel not to fear going down into Egypt, promising to make him a great nation there, go down with him and bring him up again. The household that came into Egypt is listed, and Joseph meets his father in Goshen and prepares them to speak to Pharaoh as shepherds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Jacob before he went down to Egypt?
ev: State God's three promises to Jacob in 46:3-4
Give the total number of Jacob's house who came into Egypt (46:26-27)

nodes.d: Joseph presents his brothers and father to Pharaoh, who gives them the land of Goshen to dwell in. Jacob blesses Pharaoh and describes his years as a pilgrimage, few and evil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell where Jacob's family settled in Egypt and who blessed whom in Pharaoh's court?
ev: Say what land Pharaoh gave Jacob's family and what their trade was (47:3-6)
Report what Jacob says about the years of his pilgrimage (47:9)

nodes.t: The famine and Pharaoh's ownership of the land
nodes.d: As the famine deepens Joseph gathers the money of Egypt and Canaan, then takes the people's cattle and finally their land in exchange for bread. The people become Pharaoh's servants and give a fifth of the increase, while the priests' land is not bought.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Joseph handled the famine in Egypt and what the people said in return (47:25)?
ev: List in order what the people gave Joseph for bread (47:14-20)
State the law Joseph made about the fifth part (47:26)

nodes.t: Israel's oath and the blessing of Ephraim and Manasseh
nodes.d: Israel makes Joseph swear to bury him with his fathers, then recalls God Almighty's promise at Luz and takes Ephraim and Manasseh as his own. He crosses his hands to bless the younger Ephraim first, over Joseph's objection, and says God will bring them back to the land of their fathers.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob blessed Joseph's sons and what he said God would do for the family?
ev: Say where Jacob asked to be buried and who swore to do it (47:29-31)
Explain what was unusual about the way Jacob blessed the two boys (48:13-20)

nodes.d: Jacob gathers his sons to tell what will befall them in the last days, speaking in turn to Reuben, Simeon and Levi, Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, Naphtali, Joseph and Benjamin. The chapter names these the twelve tribes of Israel; Judah's blessing is treated separately.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name at least six of Jacob's sons and say one thing Jacob said about one of them?
ev: Say what Jacob says about Reuben and why (49:3-4)
Find the verse that calls the twelve sons the tribes of Israel (49:28)

nodes.d: Jacob blesses his sons, and says the sceptre shall not depart from Judah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jacob promised Judah in Genesis 49:10?
ev: Read 49:10 and identify to whom the blessing is addressed

nodes.t: The death and burial of Jacob
nodes.d: Jacob charges his sons to bury him in the cave of Machpelah with Abraham, Isaac and their wives, and then dies. Joseph has him embalmed, Egypt mourns, and a great company goes up to Canaan to bury him there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell where Jacob was buried and why it was the same place as Abraham and Sarah?
ev: Say who is already buried in the cave according to 49:31
Describe who went up with Joseph to bury Jacob (50:7-9)

nodes.t: God meant it for good: providence
nodes.d: Joseph tells his brothers that although they meant evil, God meant it for good (50:20); Paul teaches a similar confidence in Romans 8:28.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph meant in Genesis 50:20?
ev: Explain Genesis 50:20 in context
Compare it with Romans 8:28

nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.d: Jacob's family grows into a numerous people in Egypt, and a new king who did not know Joseph sets taskmasters over them and makes their lives bitter with hard bondage. The more they are afflicted, the more they multiply.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Israel went from being Joseph's family in Egypt to being slaves, and what happened the more they were afflicted?
ev: Say why the new king feared the Israelites (1:9-10)
Describe the work they were forced to do (1:11-14)

nodes.t: Moses flees to Midian and God hears Israel's cry
nodes.d: Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, learns the deed is known, and flees to Midian, where he helps the priest's daughters and marries Zipporah. In Egypt the people groan, and God hears and remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses ended up in Midian, and what 2:23-25 says God did about Israel's cry?
ev: Say why Moses left Egypt (2:11-15)
Say what Moses did at the well in Midian (2:16-17)
Find the verse that says God remembered his covenant (2:24)

nodes.t: The firstborn die and Israel leaves Egypt
nodes.d: At midnight the LORD strikes all the firstborn in Egypt, and Pharaoh urges Israel to leave. They go with their dough unleavened, taking silver, gold and clothing given by the Egyptians, about six hundred thousand men on foot, at the end of the four hundred and thirty years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at midnight and how Israel left Egypt?
ev: Describe what happened at midnight (12:29-30)
Say what the Egyptians gave Israel (12:35-36)
Say how long the sojourning in Egypt was (12:40-41)

nodes.d: The ordinance of the Passover is set out: no foreigner or hired servant may eat of it, a bought servant who is circumcised may, the lamb is eaten in one house and no bone of it broken, and a sojourner who wants to keep it must be circumcised. One law covers native and stranger.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the Passover rules say about foreigners and about the lamb's bones?
ev: Say what is required of a stranger who wants to keep the Passover (12:48)
Say what was not to be done with the lamb's bones (12:46)

nodes.t: Led by the pillar of cloud and fire
nodes.d: God leads Israel by the wilderness way and not the near road through Philistia, lest they see war and return. Moses carries the bones of Joseph, and the LORD goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how God led Israel out of Egypt, day and night?
ev: Say why God did not lead them by the nearest road (13:17)
Describe how the LORD led them by day and by night (13:21-22)

nodes.d: The LORD calls by name Bezalel of the tribe of Judah and fills him with the spirit of God in wisdom and workmanship, and gives Aholiab of Dan and others to help make the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who God appointed to build the tabernacle and what equipped him?
ev: Say who was called and what filled him (31:2-3)
Say what he was to make (31:7-11)

nodes.d: Exodus follows the sabbath from the manna (16) through the fourth commandment (20:8-11), the law for rest (23:12), and its description as a sign and perpetual covenant (31:12-17) to a final reminder before building the tabernacle (35:1-3).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} trace what Exodus says about the sabbath from the manna to chapter 31?
ev: Say what the fourth commandment says is the reason for the sabbath (20:11)
Say what 31:13 says the sabbath is a sign of

nodes.d: God tells Moses the people have corrupted themselves and he will consume them and make a great nation of Moses. Moses pleads that the LORD brought them out and remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, and the LORD repents of the evil he thought to do.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Moses pleaded for Israel and what he asked God to remember?
ev: Say what God threatened (32:9-10)
Say what Moses asked God to remember (32:13)
Say what the LORD did in response (32:14)

nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.d: After Moses dies, the LORD tells Joshua to lead the people over the Jordan, promises to be with him, and charges him to keep the law; Joshua then orders the people to prepare and the eastern tribes pledge their help.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God said to Joshua at the start of the book?
ev: Retell what the LORD told Joshua after Moses died
Say what Joshua was told to do with the book of the law (1:7-8)
Explain what Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh promised (1:12-18)

nodes.t: Cities for the Levites and the promises kept
nodes.d: The Levites receive forty-eight cities from the tribes by lot, and the chapter ends by saying the LORD gave Israel all the land he swore to their fathers, gave them rest, and not one good word failed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Joshua 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises?
ev: Say why the Levites got cities rather than a tribal territory (21:2)
Say what 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises

nodes.t: Choose this day: the covenant at Shechem
nodes.d: At Shechem Joshua recounts God's acts from Abraham to the conquest, urges Israel to choose whom to serve, makes a covenant with the people, and sets up a stone of witness before dying at 110.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Shechem and what Joshua said about choosing whom to serve?
ev: Say what Joshua and his house decided (24:15)
Retell the history Joshua recounted (24:2-13)
Say what Joshua did that day and where he was buried (24:25-30)

nodes.d: Matthew begins by tracing Jesus Christ as son of David and son of Abraham through three sets of fourteen generations, naming Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and Bathsheba along the way.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Matthew starts with Abraham and David?
ev: Say whose son Jesus is called in 1:1
Name the three groups of fourteen generations (1:17)

nodes.d: Tested by Pharisees, Jesus points back to male and female at the beginning and “one flesh”, says what God joined man must not separate, speaks of Moses’ allowance because of hard hearts, and says not all can receive the saying about eunuchs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about marriage and why?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from the beginning
Explain why Moses allowed divorce according to 19:8

nodes.t: Woes on the scribes and Pharisees
nodes.d: Jesus tells the crowds to do what the scribes and Pharisees say but not what they do, warns against titles and pride, pronounces seven woes for hypocrisy, and laments over Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus criticised in the scribes and Pharisees?
ev: List several hypocrisies Jesus names
Describe the lament over Jerusalem (23:37-39)

nodes.t: Watch, for no one knows the day
nodes.d: Jesus says no one but the Father knows the day, compares the coming to the days of Noah, and tells disciples to watch and be ready, with the picture of the faithful and evil servant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus told his disciples to be ready?
ev: State who knows the day and hour
Contrast the faithful and the evil servant

nodes.t: Marriage and divorce, and blessing the children
nodes.d: Tested about divorce, Jesus points to creation: male and female, leaving father and mother and becoming one flesh; later he welcomes children, saying the kingdom of God belongs to such and must be received as a child.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught about marriage and about children?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from creation about marriage
Explain what he says about the children

nodes.d: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus so he may know the certainty of what he was taught, from the births of John and Jesus to the resurrection, ascension and the apostles' commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Luke wrote his Gospel and where it begins and ends?
ev: Say who Luke addresses, why he wrote, and how the book begins and ends.

nodes.d: Elisabeth bears a son, the family insists on the name John, Zacharias's tongue is loosed, and he blesses God for the horn of salvation, the oath to Abraham, and his son who will go before the Lord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Zacharias spoke again and what he said about John and God's promise?
ev: Describe how Zacharias regained speech and what he said about God's covenant and about John.

nodes.t: Woes on the Pharisees and Lawyers
nodes.d: At a Pharisee's table Jesus rebukes the Pharisees for cleaning the outside while inside is full of wickedness and tithing herbs while neglecting judgment and the love of God, and the lawyers for burdening men and building the prophets' tombs; the scribes begin to lie in wait for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the faults Jesus names in the Pharisees and lawyers?
ev: List some things Jesus faults the Pharisees and lawyers for.

nodes.t: The Kingdom's Coming and the Days of the Son of Man
nodes.d: Asked when the kingdom comes, Jesus says it does not come with observation and is in the midst of them, then tells the disciples the Son of man will be revealed suddenly like lightning, as in the days of Noe and Lot, after he first suffers and is rejected.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus compares his coming to the days of Noe and Lot?
ev: Say how Jesus describes the coming of the Son of man and what examples he uses.

nodes.t: John: Believe That Jesus Is the Christ
nodes.d: John presents Jesus as the Word made flesh through signs, 'I am' sayings, a farewell discourse, the cross and resurrection, and states that these things are written so readers believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and have life in his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why John wrote his Gospel and how it begins and ends?
ev: State why John says he wrote the book and name some signs or 'I am' sayings.

nodes.d: John opens with the Word, who was in the beginning with God and was God, through whom all things were made, who is life and light, and who became flesh and dwelt among us full of grace and truth; John the Baptist is sent to witness to the light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John 1 teaches about who the Word is and what he did?
ev: Say what John says about the Word before creation, in creation and in becoming flesh.

nodes.d: Andrew and another follow Jesus, Andrew brings Simon who is named Cephas, Philip finds Nathanael, who confesses Jesus the Son of God and King of Israel, and Jesus says they will see angels ascending and descending on the Son of man.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the first disciples Jesus gathered and what Nathanael said about him?
ev: Name the first disciples called and what Nathanael confessed.

nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.d: Peter tells the amazed crowd that the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up, and that faith in his name made the man strong. He calls them to repent so that their sins may be blotted out, and reminds them of God's covenant with the fathers and the blessing promised to Abraham's seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said made the man walk and what he urged the crowd to do?
ev: Say whom Peter credits for the healing (3:12-16)
Explain what Peter calls the people to do and why (3:18-19, 3:25-26)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Abraham, the patriarchs and Joseph
nodes.d: Asked by the high priest if the charges are true, Stephen begins with the God of glory appearing to Abraham, the promise of the land, the covenant of circumcision and the sons of Jacob. He tells how the patriarchs sold Joseph in envy, yet God was with him and raised him up in Egypt, and how Jacob and his family came down there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how Stephen begins his speech from Abraham to Joseph?
ev: Say what God promised Abraham and how long his seed would be in a strange land (7:3-7)
Retell what Stephen says about Joseph and his brothers (7:9-14)

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham to show that righteousness is counted to the one who believes, before circumcision, and that Abraham is the father of all who believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 4 uses Genesis 15:6?
ev: Link Romans 4:3 to Genesis 15:6
Explain why it matters that Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision (4:9-12)

nodes.d: As sin and death came into the world through one man, so grace and righteousness come through one man, Jesus Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contrast between Adam and Christ in Romans 5?
ev: Compare Adam and Christ in 5:15-19
Connect 5:12 to Genesis 3

nodes.d: God works all things for good to those who love him, and those he foreknew he predestined, called, justified and glorified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the steps of Romans 8:29-30?
ev: List the steps in 8:29-30 in order

nodes.d: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?
ev: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
Explain 9:15-16

nodes.t: Your body is the Lord's temple
nodes.d: Paul teaches that the body is for the Lord, not for sexual immorality, that believers are members of Christ and the Spirit's temple, and that they were bought with a price.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says our bodies belong to God, using 1 Corinthians 6:19-20?
ev: Explain why the body is not for fornication (6:13-15)
Say what Paul tells them to do about fornication (6:18)
Explain what it means that believers are bought with a price (6:19-20)

nodes.t: The resurrection body and the victory over death
nodes.d: Paul answers how the dead are raised, with the picture of a seed, contrasts the natural and spiritual body and the first and last Adam, and describes believers being changed at the last trumpet with death swallowed up in victory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Paul says will happen to the dead in Christ and to the living, using 1 Corinthians 15:42-58?
ev: Explain the seed picture (15:36-38)
Contrast sown and raised in 15:42-44
Explain how believers will be changed (15:51-53)
State the closing exhortation of 15:58

nodes.d: Paul's second letter to the Corinthians: comfort in affliction, the ministry of the new covenant and reconciliation, the collection for the saints, and a defence of his apostleship (1:1-13:14).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of 2 Corinthians and say what its three main parts are about?
ev: Name the main sections: comfort and ministry (1-7), the collection (8-9), Paul's defence of his apostleship (10-13)
Say what Paul tells the Corinthians about his sufferings

nodes.d: Paul says the gospel is the light of the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Christ, hidden to those blinded by the god of this world, and that believers carry it in weak earthen vessels so that the power is God's.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says we have this treasure in earthen vessels (2 Corinthians 4:7)?
ev: Explain who blinds unbelievers and why (4:4)
Say where the light of the knowledge of God's glory is seen (4:6)
Explain why we have the treasure in earthen vessels (4:7)
Describe the four contrasts in 4:8-9

nodes.t: False apostles and Paul's foolish boasting
nodes.d: Paul fears the Corinthians will be led astray from Christ as the serpent deceived Eve, warns of false apostles disguised as servants of righteousness, and, speaking as a fool, lists his sufferings as a servant of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul warns about false apostles in 2 Corinthians 11:13-15 and why he lists his sufferings?
ev: Say what Paul fears in 11:3
Explain how false apostles disguise themselves (11:13-15)
List some sufferings Paul names in 11:23-27
Describe the escape at Damascus (11:32-33)

nodes.d: Paul writes to the churches of Galatia, who were turning to another gospel, to defend justification by faith, the freedom of the sons of God and life by the Spirit (1:1-6:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul wrote to the Galatians and what he says the true gospel is?
ev: Say what problem prompted the letter (1:6-9)
Name the three parts: Paul's defence (1-2), justification by faith (3-4), living by the Spirit (5-6)

nodes.t: Abraham, faith and the blessing for the nations
nodes.d: Paul argues that Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness, so those of faith are Abraham's children, and that Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law so that the blessing of Abraham might come to the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Galatians 3:6-9 connects Abraham's faith to the Gentiles?
ev: Quote what Paul says Abraham did (3:6)
Explain who are the children of Abraham (3:7)
Say what the scripture foresaw (3:8)
Explain how Christ redeemed us from the curse (3:13-14)

nodes.d: Paul argues that the promise to Abraham and his seed, who is Christ, cannot be cancelled by the law that came 430 years later, and that the law was added because of transgressions until the seed should come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says the law relates to the promise made to Abraham in Galatians 3:15-22?
ev: Explain why the law does not cancel the promise (3:15-18)
Say who the seed is (3:16)
Say why the law was added (3:19)
Say what the scripture has concluded about all (3:22)

nodes.t: Two sons, two covenants: Hagar and Sarah
nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham's two sons, one by the bondwoman and one by the free woman, as an allegory of two covenants, and says believers are children of promise like Isaac and not children of the bondwoman.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul reads the story of Hagar and Sarah in Galatians 4:21-31?
ev: Say who the two sons and their mothers are (4:22-23)
Explain the two covenants named in 4:24-26
Say who Paul says we are like (4:28, 4:31)
Quote the scripture Paul cites in 4:30

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the saints at Ephesus: God's blessings in Christ, salvation by grace, the unity of Jew and Gentile in one body, and how to walk worthy in the church, home and spiritual battle (1:1-6:24).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Ephesians and say what its two halves are about?
ev: Describe the two halves: what God has done in Christ (1-3) and how to walk worthy (4-6)

nodes.t: Marriage and Christ and the church
nodes.d: Paul instructs wives and husbands, grounding the husband's love and the wife's submission in the relation of Christ to the church, quotes the scripture about two becoming one flesh, and calls this a great mystery concerning Christ and the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul connects marriage with Christ and the church in Ephesians 5:22-33?
ev: Say what Paul commands wives and husbands (5:22, 5:25)
Describe what Christ did for the church (5:25-27)
Say what Paul says the "great mystery" is about (5:32)

nodes.d: Paul writes to the church at Colosse about the supremacy of Christ, warns against empty philosophy and rules, and calls believers raised with Christ to a new life (1:1-4:18).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short outline of Colossians and say who Paul says Christ is?
ev: Describe the main sections: the supremacy of Christ (1), warnings (2), the new life (3-4)

nodes.d: Paul says Christ is the image of the invisible God, firstborn of creation, by whom and for whom all things were created, head of the church and firstborn from the dead, in whom all fulness dwells and through whose cross God reconciles all things.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Colossians 1:15-20 says about who Christ is?
ev: List what Paul says Christ is and has done in 1:15-20
Explain how the Colossians were reconciled (1:21-22)
Say the condition stated in 1:23

nodes.t: A rest remains for the people of God
nodes.d: The promise of entering God's rest still stands: the gospel preached to them did not profit those without faith, God rested on the seventh day, and a Sabbath rest remains for God's people, so they must labour to enter it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the rest is that remains for God's people, and what warning goes with it (4:9-11)?
ev: Cite the creation rest mentioned in 4:4
State what remains for the people of God (4:9)
Say what the word of God does in 4:12

nodes.t: God's oath to Abraham: an anchor of the soul
nodes.d: God promised Abraham and confirmed it by an oath, swearing by himself; by two unchangeable things the heirs of promise have strong comfort, a hope like an anchor that enters within the veil where Jesus has gone as forerunner, a high priest after Melchizedek's order.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the text says about God's promise and oath to Abraham, and why it gives us hope (6:13-19)?
ev: State why God swore by himself (6:13)
Describe the anchor picture of 6:19-20

nodes.t: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest
nodes.d: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, met Abraham, blessed him and received tithes; this shows he is greater than Abraham and the Levites, and is made like the Son of God, abiding a priest continually.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Hebrews 7:1-10 says about Melchizedek and why he is called greater than Abraham?
ev: Retell how 7:1-2 summarises Genesis 14
Explain the argument that the lesser is blessed by the greater (7:7)

nodes.t: What faith is: Abel, Enoch and Noah
nodes.d: Faith is the substance of things hoped for and evidence of things unseen; by faith Abel offered a better sacrifice, Enoch was translated, and Noah built the ark; without faith it is impossible to please God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what faith is (11:1) and give the example of Noah (11:7)?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 11:1
Say what 11:6 requires of one who comes to God
Name what each of Abel, Enoch and Noah did by faith

nodes.t: By faith Abraham, Sarah and the patriarchs
nodes.d: By faith Abraham went out not knowing where, sojourned as a stranger seeking a city built by God, Sara received strength to bear a child, Abraham offered Isaac, and Isaac, Jacob and Joseph acted in faith about things to come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Abraham did by faith and what the patriarchs were looking for (11:8-16)?
ev: Say what Abraham did by faith in 11:8-10 and 11:17-19
Name what Isaac, Jacob and Joseph did in 11:20-22
State what 11:13-16 says these people sought

nodes.t: Pursue peace and holiness; the example of Esau
nodes.d: The readers are to follow peace and holiness, watch against a root of bitterness, and not be like Esau, who sold his birthright for one meal and later found no place of repentance though he sought the blessing with tears.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the writer says about Esau as a warning (12:15-17)?
ev: Say what we are to follow (12:14)
Tell what Esau did and what happened afterward (12:16-17)

nodes.t: Not Mount Sinai but Mount Zion
nodes.d: Believers have not come to the fearful mountain of Sinai but to mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, to God, to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant and to the blood of sprinkling; they must not refuse the one who speaks, and receive a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Hebrews 12:18-24 contrasts Sinai with Zion and names Jesus there?
ev: Contrast the two mountains (12:18-24)
State what is said of the kingdom and of God (12:28-29)

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.d: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?
ev: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3

nodes.d: 1 Peter is a letter from the apostle Peter to scattered strangers in Asia Minor, written to encourage them in suffering with the living hope, the example of Christ, holy conduct and humility under God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how 1 Peter encourages believers who suffer?
ev: Say who wrote 1 Peter and to whom
Name the main themes: hope, holiness, suffering and humility

nodes.t: Wives, husbands and the hidden person of the heart
nodes.d: Peter addresses wives with the example of Sarah and holy women, stressing a meek and quiet spirit as precious to God, and tells husbands to live with their wives with understanding and honour as fellow heirs of the grace of life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Peter tells husbands and wives in 1 Peter 3:1-7?
ev: Say what Peter calls the adorning of great price
Describe what husbands are told in 3:7

nodes.t: Christ suffered once, the days of Noah and baptism
nodes.d: Peter says Christ suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, to bring us to God, and was made alive; he mentions the spirits who were disobedient in the days of Noah, the eight saved by water, and says baptism saves by the resurrection of Jesus, who is now at God's right hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Peter 3:18-22 says about Christ and about Noah?
ev: Say why Christ suffered once according to 3:18
Retell what 3:20 says about Noah and the eight saved through water
State where Christ is now according to 3:22

nodes.d: 2 Peter is a letter from Simon Peter urging growth in the knowledge of Christ, warning against false teachers and scoffers, and pointing to the certain day of the Lord and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 2 Peter warns about and what it tells believers to do?
ev: Name the three sections: growth, false teachers, the day of the Lord
Say what Peter wants believers to remember

nodes.t: False teachers and the examples of judgment
nodes.d: Peter warns that false teachers will bring in destructive heresies out of covetousness, and shows that God judged sinning angels, the old world in Noah's day, and Sodom and Gomorrah while delivering Noah and Lot.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what examples Peter uses to show God judges the ungodly and rescues the godly?
ev: Describe what the false teachers do and why
List the three examples of judgment in 2:4-6
Say who God delivered in 2:5-9

nodes.t: Scoffers and the longsuffering of the Lord
nodes.d: Peter says scoffers will ask where the promised coming is, recalls that the world once perished by water and the present heavens and earth are kept for fire, and says the Lord delays because he is longsuffering, not willing that any perish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Peter says the Lord seems slow to keep his promise?
ev: Say what the scoffers claim in 3:4
Explain what Peter says they forget in 3:5-7
Say why the Lord has not yet come, according to 3:9

nodes.d: 1 John is a letter written so that believers may have fellowship with the Father and the Son, know they have eternal life, walk in the light, love one another, and hold to the truth that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 1 John wants believers to know?
ev: Name the main themes: light, love, truth about Jesus, assurance
Say what John says he wrote so that in 5:13

nodes.t: Love in deed and truth, assurance and the commandment
nodes.d: John says love is the message from the beginning, unlike Cain who killed his brother, that Christ laid down his life for us so we ought to love in deed and truth, and that God is greater than a condemning heart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what John means by loving not in word only but in deed and in truth?
ev: Say how John contrasts Cain with the love Christ showed
Explain what loving in deed and truth means in 3:17-18
State the commandment in 3:23

nodes.d: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered, warns of ungodly men who crept in, recalls examples of judgment, and ends with a call to keep in God's love and a doxology.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Jude asks believers to contend for?
ev: Say who wrote Jude
Say what Jude urges in verse 3

nodes.t: Examples of judgment: unbelievers, angels and Sodom
nodes.d: Jude recalls that the Lord destroyed those who did not believe after saving a people out of Egypt, that angels who left their place are kept in chains until judgment, and that Sodom and Gomorrha suffer the vengeance of eternal fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the three examples of judgment Jude gives?
ev: List the three examples in verses 5-7
Say what Sodom and Gomorrha are set forth as

nodes.t: The ungodly men described: Cain, Balaam, Core and Enoch's prophecy
nodes.d: Jude says these dreamers despise authority, have gone in the way of Cain, the error of Balaam and the rebellion of Core, are like waterless clouds and fruitless trees, and that Enoch prophesied the Lord comes to judge the ungodly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the false men in Jude using the examples and pictures Jude gives?
ev: Say what Jude says about Michael in verse 9
Name the three figures in verse 11
Describe the pictures from nature in verses 12-13
Say what Enoch prophesied in verses 14-15

nodes.d: Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ given to John on Patmos: letters to seven churches, a vision of the throne in heaven, the Lamb, series of seals, trumpets and bowls, and the end in the new Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the main parts of Revelation as the book itself presents them?
ev: Say who gave the revelation and to whom
Name the main parts: churches, throne, Lamb, judgments, new heaven and earth
Say what is promised to the one who reads and keeps it in 1:3

nodes.t: The sealed scroll and the Lamb
nodes.d: John weeps that no one can open the sealed scroll until the Lion of the tribe of Juda appears as a Lamb as though slain, takes the scroll, and heaven and every creature worship him as worthy because he redeemed people from every nation by his blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is worthy to open the scroll and why?
ev: Say why John wept and what was announced
Describe the Lamb and what he does
Say what the new song says about why he is worthy

nodes.t: The woman, the dragon and the man child
nodes.d: John sees a woman clothed with the sun who bears a man child who is caught up to God, a great red dragon who tries to devour the child, war in heaven in which the dragon is cast down, and the dragon's pursuit of the woman and her seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the main figures of Revelation 12 and what the text says each does?
ev: Describe the woman, the dragon and the child
Say who the dragon is named in 12:9
Say how the saints overcome him in 12:11
Describe what the dragon does after he is cast down

nodes.t: The river of life and the tree of life
nodes.d: John sees the river of the water of life from the throne of God and of the Lamb, with the tree of life on either side bearing twelve fruits and healing the nations, no more curse, and the servants seeing God's face and reigning for ever.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Revelation 22:1-5 says is in the city?
ev: Describe the river and the tree
Say what 22:3 says about the curse
Say what God's servants do according to 22:3-5
